goal: Every pull request here should say whether it carries a change record, so this repo starts getting the brief, the kept evidence and release notes that agent-kit's debrief skill writes.
changed: New workflow .github/workflows/changes.yml runs agent-kit's debrief.py check --base on every pull request, in observe mode.
It reports a pull request that changes a file outside the bookkeeping files and adds no record. It never fails one.
The checker is its own pinned checkout of agent-kit (main after #74). The pins the other checks use are untouched.
This is the first record in .changes/.

claims.claim: The command the workflow runs reports a pull request with no record, exits 0 in observe mode, and passes once a good record is committed.
claims.check: debrief.py check --base origin/main --root . --observe on this branch, with agent-kit at 951bae9 and /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6 on macOS: before the record it printed the would-have-failed line, after it printed 1 record checked, 0 with problems
claims.remaining: The workflow file itself: its two checkouts, the sparse checkout and the base ref on a GitHub runner.

claims.claim: The workflow runs in GitHub Actions on a pull request and does not fail it.
claims.remaining: This pull request's own run is the first. Read the step's log there.

claims.claim: The checks this repo already runs still pass with a .changes/ folder in the tree.
claims.check: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (the suite the test workflow records) and ledger verify
claims.remaining: Run locally on macOS, not on the runner. CI on this pull request repeats them.

next.item: Drop --observe so a pull request with no record fails
next.why_now: Not yet. agent-kit is watching the same check for a week to see if docs-only pull requests make it noisy, and this repo should follow its answer.
next.impact: Until then a pull request with no record still merges and the miss shows only in the CI log. 22 of 25 of this repo's recent merged pull requests would have needed a record.

next.item: Print release notes for this repo with debrief.py notes
next.why_now: Only useful once a few records with a release note exist, so after the next handful of pull requests.
next.impact: You get a dated list of what changed for a user of this repo, which it has never had.

release.none: CI only; nothing changes for a user of this repo
